paragraphs: Here's what I love about Caleb, friend. He didn't ask for the easy land. He asked for the hill country, where the Anakim lived in great and fortified cities, and he asked at eighty-five years old, because the LORD had promised it (Joshua 14:12).

The passage says it twice: Caleb "wholly followed the LORD" (Joshua 14:9, 14). The LORD kept him alive for forty-five years, and at eighty-five he says he's still as strong as the day Moses sent him out (Joshua 14:10-11). Notice how Caleb talks, too: "Perhaps with the LORD's help I will drive them out" (Joshua 14:12). His strength was real, but his hope sat in the LORD.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Following God all the way is a long game, and a promise from Him is worth holding onto even when the wait feels longer than a Monday. Caleb's story says the LORD notices faithfulness, and Joshua blessed him and gave him Hebron (Joshua 14:13). You don't have to be the loudest or the youngest, so just keep following Him wholly and let Him handle the giants.
